'''Kuno Kokuzō''' (久努国造) refers to the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kokuzō}} of Kuno Province, located in the central region of {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|en|Tōtōmi Province|qid=Q1048864|lt=Tōtōmi Province}}.

== Overview ==

=== Name ===
The name is recorded as **Kuno Kokuzō** in the ''{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}'', "Kokuzō Hongi" section.

=== Ancestors ===
* According to the ''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Inaba Sukune (印幡足尼), a grandson of {{ill|Ikagashiko-o|ja|伊香色雄|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55536799}} of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|Mononobe clan|qid=Q1755836|lt=Mononobe clan}}, was appointed Kokuzō during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}}.
* The ''Tenson Hongi'' and ''Kokuzō Hongi'' also mention Inagimi Ren Kimi (印岐美連公), a son of Ikashikone-no-mikoto or {{ill|Mononobe no Tokone|ja|物部十千根|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24885356}}, as an ancestor of the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|ja|志紀県主}}, Tōtōmi Kokuzō, Kuno Nao, and Saya Nao.<ref>Toshio Hōga, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/hitori/takaosan1.htm Preservation Issues of Takao-san Kofun in Numazu]," ''Kojiki no Homma,'' 2015.</ref>

=== Clan ===
The clan was called the **Kuno clan** (久能氏) with the surname Nao (直) and was related to the {{ill|Saya clan|ja|佐夜氏}}.

== Headquarters ==
The Kokuzō's base was in the Kuno Province, later known as {{ill|Yamana district|ja|山名郡|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11467644}}, specifically in the areas now called {{ill|Kuno village|ja|久努郷}}, near modern {{ill|Fukuroi, Shizuoka|en|Fukuroi, Shizuoka|qid=Q821337|lt=Fukuroi, Shizuoka}} in Washizu and Kuno.<ref>Masato Shimonaka, "Yamana District," in ''Shizuoka Prefecture Place Names,'' {{ill|Heibonsha|en|Heibonsha|qid=Q11482108|lt=Heibonsha}}, 2000.</ref>

=== Territory ===
The Kuno Kokuzō ruled over the Kuno Province, covering Yamana District (modern Fukuroi), {{ill|Shūchi District, Shizuoka|en|Shūchi District, Shizuoka|qid=Q1205501|lt=Shuchi District, Shizuoka}}, and {{ill|Saya district|ja|佐野郡|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11385111}}. Some theories suggest neighboring {{ill|Q85883175|ja|素賀国造|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q85883175}} were based in Sano District, but historical records indicate Yamana District was formed in 722 AD by separating eight villages from Sano District, confirming the Kuno Kokuzō ruled both districts.<ref>Shimonaka, "Sano District," in ''Shizuoka Prefecture Place Names,'' Heibonsha, 2000.</ref>

== Clan Deity ==
The clan deity was likely worshiped at {{ill|Akao Shibutare Kōribe Shrine|ja|赤尾渋垂郡辺神社|qid=Q117452953}},<ref>Toshio Hōga, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keijiban/kunosi.htm The Kuno and Hara Clans]," ''Kojiki no Homma,'' 2002.</ref> which enshrines Ikagimi-no-mikoto.

=== Related Shrines ===
* {{ill|Nanatsumori Shrine|ja|七ツ森神社|qid=Q134957351}}
: Located in Kuno, Fukuroi, this shrine enshrines the Kuno Kokuzō.

=== Tombs ===
* {{ill|Zao Gongen Shrine Kofun|ja|蔵王権現神社古墳|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506354}}
: A 49-meter-long, 4-meter-high {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qid=Q1141225}}, dated to the 4th century and believed to be the tomb of Inaba Sukune.<ref>Hōga, "Preservation Issues of Takao-san Kofun," 2015.</ref>
* {{ill|Wadaoka Kofun Group|ja|和田岡古墳群|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506356}}
** {{ill|Kakuwakanatsuka Kofun|ja|各和金塚古墳|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506358}}: A 66-meter-long {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} from the early 5th century.
** {{ill|Hisagotuka Kofun|ja|瓢塚古墳}}: A 63-meter-long zenpō-kōen-fun from the early 5th century.
** {{ill|Gyōnintuka Kofun|ja|行人塚古墳|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506359}}: A 43-meter-long zenpō-kōen-fun dated to the 4th or 5th century.
** {{ill|Yoshioka Ōtsuka Kofun|ja|吉岡大塚古墳|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135506361}}: A 55-meter-long zenpō-kōen-fun from the mid-5th century.
